problem_statement: The SubhanRaj News-Website-Template project is a runnable Bootstrap 4 static editorial/news site already rebranded as the Harbor Ledger, an independent coastal daily out of the fictional Wrackline Harbor, with a fixed masthead and category navigation, a home page of top-stories and featured headlines, a news-details lead article (single-news-1.html) and an archive page (archive.html). Grow the paper's coastal-desk idea into a shared 'Harbor tide board' design-system component: add a tide board section (eyebrow 'HARBOR TIDE BOARD', a desk filter with four chips — All desks / Harbourfront / Fleet & catch / Weather watch — and a live 'Showing N desks' status readout) plus a shared 'tide rail' to the footer region of EVERY graded page (home, lead article, archive) so readers can jump to a coastal desk from anywhere. The tide rail must appear consistently on all three pages, not only on the home page. Wire the desk filter end to end: clicking a desk chip (Fleet & catch / Weather watch) must update the '.tide-status' readout to reflect the selected desk (e.g. clicking Fleet & catch sets 'Showing 1 desk: fleet and catch.'), not merely highlight the chip and hide the desk rows. The tide board and rail must keep the airy Harbor Ledger newsroom look (paper-white panels, navy #16324f text, teal-slate #2e6b7d accent, Roboto headings) matching the masthead, and must be responsive so the home page has NO horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile viewport. Preserve the Harbor Ledger identity, the category navigation, the top-stories and featured headlines, the lead article, the archive grid, the local images, and the desktop/tablet layout.
required_content: Add the Harbor tide board component (eyebrow 'HARBOR TIDE BOARD', heading 'Today on the Wrackline Harbor desks', the four desk chips All desks / Harbourfront / Fleet & catch / Weather watch, and a '.tide-status' 'Showing N desks' readout) into the footer region of the home page.

Add the shared 'tide rail' (eyebrow 'HARBOR TIDE BOARD' + coastal desk links) to the footer region of ALL THREE graded pages — the home page, the lead article (single-news-1.html), and the archive (archive.html) — so the same shared component appears consistently site-wide, not only on the home page.

Style the tide board's desk-filter strip and the shared rail to match the Harbor Ledger newsroom look (paper-white panels, navy text, teal-slate accent, Roboto headings) — the rendered tide board must be visually faithful to the reference, not a collapsed or off-palette (dark/charcoal) restyle.

Make the desk-filter strip responsive so the home page has NO horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile viewport (allow the chips to wrap / use a fluid layout instead of a fixed-width non-wrapping row). Do not merely clip the overflow with overflow-x:hidden; the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport width.
Keep the desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts free of horizontal overflow.

Wire the desk filter fully end to end: clicking a desk chip (Fleet & catch / Weather watch / All desks) must update the '.tide-status' readout to reflect the selected desk (e.g. clicking Fleet & catch yields 'Showing 1 desk: fleet and catch.'), in addition to highlighting the active chip and hiding the non-matching desk rows — the post-click terminal state must reflect the selected desk, not the default 'Showing 3 desks'.

Do not damage the existing Harbor Ledger masthead, category navigation, top-stories, featured headlines, the lead article, the archive grid, the local images, or the footer credit; keep the 'Independent coastal journalism from Wrackline Harbor' identity on every page.
design_constraints: Keep the airy Harbor Ledger newsroom visual language: paper-white/light backgrounds, navy #16324f text, teal-slate #2e6b7d accent, Roboto headings / Open Sans body, the fixed masthead and category nav.
Do not replace the news site, the tide board, or the pages with a new app shell, framework, external design system, or unrelated layout.

Do not remove the tide board, the four desk chips, the shared footer tide rail, the top-stories, the featured headlines, the lead article, the archive grid, the category navigation, or the filter script.
Do not add npm dependencies, remote scripts, remote fonts, remote images, generated build outputs, or unrelated file churn.

The tide board's desk-filter strip and the rail must fit within 1440px desktop, 834px tablet, and 390px mobile viewports without horizontal overflow, and must render in the Harbor Ledger newsroom palette.
state_constraints: desktop_home anchors the reframed masthead, the top story, and the Harbor tide board component.

desktop_tideboard scrolls the tide board into view: it must render in the airy newsroom palette (paper-white panel, navy text, teal-slate chips) faithful to the reference, not a collapsed off-palette strip.
desktop_fleet_filter clicks the Fleet & catch chip: the '.tide-status' readout must then read 'Showing 1 desk: fleet and catch.' (the post-click terminal state reflects the selected desk).
desktop_article and desktop_archive verify the shared tide rail appears on the lead article and the archive footers, not only on the home page, and that the Harbor Ledger coastal identity survives.

change_completion: The Harbor tide board and its four desk chips are present on the home page.
The shared tide rail appears in the footer region of all three pages (home, article, archive).
On mobile the home page has no horizontal overflow after the responsive layout.
design_consistency: The tide-board desk-filter strip and shared rail keep the airy Harbor Ledger newsroom style and are visually faithful to the reference.
The same tide-board component is consistent across all three pages; the masthead, top-stories, and imagery remain recognizable.
regression: Home, article, and archive pages retain the Harbor Ledger branding, category nav, headlines, and imagery.
No new dependency, remote asset, generated build artifact, or broad redesign is introduced.
responsive: The home page has no horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile states.
Desktop and tablet states remain free of horizontal overflow.

author_notes: Grow the Harbor Ledger coastal daily into a shared 'Harbor tide board' design-system component: a desk-filter tide board on the home page plus a shared tide rail on the footer of home, lead article, and archive, keeping the newsroom palette (paper-white panels, navy #16324f, teal-slate #2e6b7d, Roboto), the desk-filter '.tide-status' readout wired end to end, and no mobile horizontal overflow. The remote Google-Fonts @import removal is supplied as infrastructure identically in all legs.

The remote Google-Fonts @import removal is supplied as infrastructure in all legs.
